heading.en: A notice he would not obey

hook.en: The government orders Gandhi to leave Champaran at once. He calmly writes that he will not go, and thousands of peasants gather outside the court.

objectives.en: Explain Gandhi's act of civil disobedience
Describe how the case ended and why it mattered

narration.en: The government orders Gandhi to leave Champaran at once. He calmly writes that he will not go, and thousands of peasants gather outside the court.

body.en: Gandhi first tried to get the facts. He met the secretary of the British landlords' association, who refused to give information to an outsider, and the British official commissioner of the Tirhut division, who tried to bully him into leaving. Gandhi then went to Motihari, the capital of Champaran, to start his inquiry with lawyers' help.

points.en: Visits the commissioner of Tirhut division
Is told to leave, but goes to Motihari

say.en: The commissioner tries to bully Gandhi into leaving Tirhut.
Gandhi goes instead to Motihari, the capital of Champaran.
He is served a notice to quit and writes that he will disobey.

text.en: Notice to quit; he refuses in writing

say.en: Thousands of peasants crowd around the court in support.
Gandhi pleads guilty, saying he follows the higher law of conscience.
The government drops the case. Civil disobedience has triumphed.

body.en: On his way to a village where a peasant had been mistreated, Gandhi was served an official notice to quit Champaran at once. He signed the receipt and wrote on it that he would disobey. When he was summoned to court, thousands of peasants gathered spontaneously outside. The officials were helpless without his cooperation. Gandhi pleaded guilty, saying he was following the higher law of conscience. Within days the case was dropped.

points.en: Ordered to leave Champaran; he refuses in writing
Thousands of peasants gather at the court
Pleads guilty, citing the voice of conscience
The case is dropped: civil disobedience wins

narration.en: On his way to a village where a peasant had been mistreated, Gandhi was served an official notice to quit Champaran at once. He signed the receipt and wrote on it that he would disobey. When he was summoned to court, thousands of peasants gathered spontaneously outside.

problem.en: Why is the Champaran episode considered a turning point in Gandhi's life?

steps.en: Context: poor indigo sharecroppers exploited by English planters.
Action: he disobeyed an order to leave and pleaded guilty, citing conscience.
Result: the case was dropped; peasants lost their fear.
Meaning: civil disobedience had worked in India; the British could not order him about in his own country.

answer.en: At Champaran, Gandhi first used civil disobedience on Indian soil and won. The peasants lost their fear of the British, and Gandhi himself called it a turning point in his life.
